summary.headline: All 3 §8-E hook trait surfaces are present + sealed-discipline preserved + Class B β intact + InstallPorts.policy port shape (CRITIC-2 F-1.2) honored. The S3a InstallConsentPolicy threading is wired AT THE PORT LEVEL but no engine-side adapter exists to project CapabilityPolicy::check_install_consent into the install_plugin call path — the only production-reachable InstallConsentPolicy impl is AdmitAllInstallConsent. A custom CapabilityPolicy that overrides check_install_consent has ZERO runtime effect at v1-beta unless an adapter lands. The V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md row claim 'external policy authors overriding any of the three hooks now have runtime effect at v1-beta' is true for §S3b (per_delegation) + §S3c (check_write_with_audience) but FALSE for §S3a (install_consent) — sec-r6r2-l6-1 MAJOR. Test-shape concerns at sec-r6r2-l6-2/3/4 MINOR. R6 R1 L6 substrate-frozen-but-consumer-unwired cluster verified closed at S1/S2/S3b/S3c (consumer reachable end-to-end) and PARTIAL at S3a (consumer reachable only via test-fixture port-wiring; production CapabilityPolicy override is dead surface).
summary.convergence_signal_vs_r1: Substantial R6 R1 cluster closure (4 of 5 §S surfaces fully consumer-wired); S3a residual is the single remaining surface gap. Trend = monotonic improvement; recommend the MAJOR get an FP-2 closure (engine-side adapter ~30 LOC) or an explicit V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md Row update from 'CLOSED' to 'PARTIAL-CLOSED, adapter to G-COMP-1' so the doc + state agree.

findings.title: §S3a install-consent: engine-side adapter `CapabilityPolicyInstallConsent` is referenced in install_consent.rs:25 module doc but does not exist; production CapabilityPolicy.check_install_consent override is dead surface at v1-beta

evidence.doc_claim: crates/benten-platform-foundation/src/install_consent.rs:25 — '...the engine-side adapter `CapabilityPolicyInstallConsent` (NOT in this crate because of the dep-cycle constraint) wraps the policy.'
evidence.code_search: `git grep -ln CapabilityPolicyInstallConsent 3c80546f` returns ONLY the install_consent.rs reference (the doc-claim line itself). No `impl InstallConsentPolicy for ...` over CapabilityPolicy exists anywhere in benten-engine, benten-caps, benten-platform-foundation, bindings/napi, or packages/engine. The only production-callable InstallConsentPolicy impls are AdmitAllInstallConsent + DenyAllInstallConsent (both helpers).
evidence.v1_frozen_interface_md_line_735_contradi: docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:735 row claim 'Net: external policy authors overriding any of the three hooks now have runtime effect at v1-beta' is FALSE for check_install_consent — without the adapter, a custom CapabilityPolicy.check_install_consent is unreachable from `plugin_lifecycle::install_plugin`'s `policy: &dyn InstallConsentPolicy` port.
evidence.deferral_already_documented_inconsistent: V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md Row D-3 marks D-3-a 'CLOSED' at §S3a (line 154), then forensic body at line 200+ says 'A future custom CapabilityPolicy author overriding any of the three will be silently ignored' (which is now FALSE for §S3b/§S3c but REMAINS TRUE for §S3a). The doc-state is internally inconsistent — Row D-3-a should be 'PARTIAL CLOSED, adapter to G-COMP-1' OR the adapter should land at FP-2.
evidence.delegate_capability_contrast: `delegate_capability` in engine_caps.rs:572-587 consults `self.engine.policy.as_ref().check_per_delegation(...)` DIRECTLY against the trait method — no adapter required because engine_caps lives in benten-engine and `&self.engine.policy` IS the configured CapabilityPolicy. The same direct-consultation pattern is NOT available at the install path because `plugin_lifecycle::install_plugin` lives in benten-platform-foundation which cannot dep-cycle into benten-caps via benten-engine.

impact.security: CLAUDE.md baked-in #18 Layer-2 install-time consent admission policy (e.g. a curated-DID trust-list, an institutional ratification gate) cannot be wired through the engine's CapabilityPolicy at v1-beta. The pipeline structurally consults a default-`Ok(())`-returning AdmitAllInstallConsent helper instead. A production deployment wanting install-time policy enforcement must EITHER fork the install entry point OR construct its own InstallConsentPolicy impl + pass it directly to install_plugin (which is not the documented Phase-4-Meta-Core seam shape — the documented surface is CapabilityPolicy.check_install_consent override).
impact.doc_state_consistency: V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 8 row + V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md Row D-3-a + install_consent.rs module-doc + the SECURITY-POSTURE.md line all read like the wiring is complete; the missing adapter contradicts the surface-as-documented.
impact.audit_trail: When a real CapabilityPolicy author lands at G-COMP-1 / Phase-4-Meta-Composing and discovers their check_install_consent override has been silently ignored since v1-beta, the regression-window is the entire v1-beta release.

findings.disposition:
FIX-NOW (per HARD RULE 12) — three valid options:

(a) [PREFERRED] Land the engine-side adapter at FP-2 (≤50 LOC, ~5 LOC for the blanket impl + ~10 LOC for engine glue + ~20 LOC for a substantive end-to-end test wiring a denying CapabilityPolicy through install_plugin via the adapter). The adapter shape: `impl InstallConsentPolicy for &Arc<dyn CapabilityPolicy>` (or a newtype wrapper) lives in benten-engine; engine glue construct `InstallPorts.policy = &EngineCapabilityPolicyAdapter::new(&engine.policy)` at install boundary. Production install path documented + adapter test verifies a non-default check_install_consent reaches the install pipeline.

(b) DEFER-NAMED-NOW per HARD RULE 12 clause (b): edit docs to acknowledge the gap. V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md Row D-3-a status flips 'CLOSED' → 'PARTIAL CLOSED — adapter to G-COMP-1'. V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:735 row text edits 'external policy authors overriding any of the three hooks now have runtime effect at v1-beta' → '... two of the three hooks (check_per_delegation + check_write_with_audience) now have runtime effect at v1-beta; check_install_consent's engine-side adapter defers to G-COMP-1 per dep-cycle constraint'. install_consent.rs:25 module doc edits 'the engine-side adapter `CapabilityPolicyInstallConsent` (NOT in this crate because of the dep-cycle constraint) wraps the policy' → 'The engine-side adapter is a G-COMP-1 deliverable per the dep-cycle constraint; at v1-beta production installs route through `AdmitAllInstallConsent` (admit-all) unless the caller supplies a custom InstallConsentPolicy directly to InstallPorts.policy.' Document the named destination explicitly + add a v1-beta breaking-changes warning so policy authors know.

(c) DISAGREE: cite a Ben ratification or design constraint that makes the adapter intentionally absent — none found in the F4 design pipeline pre-work.

Recommend (a) over (b) — the adapter is small + closes the gap fully + aligns the doc-state with the SHAPE-OF-PHASE-4-META-CORE v1-beta contract.

findings.title: §S3a r6_r1_fp_f4_s3a_*.rs test has 6 arms but NONE call `install_plugin(...)` end-to-end with a DenyAllInstallConsent through InstallPorts.policy
